q: There are two main ways of forming chemical bonds between atoms: ionic bonding and ____ bonding.
e: There are two main ways of forming chemical bonds between atoms: ionic bonding and covalent bonding. A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs.

q: There is another important type of chemical bonding, called ____ bonding, which is only found in metals.
e: There is another important type of chemical bonding, called metallic bonding, which is only found in metals. Metallic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: The electronic structures of noble gases are very stable and unreactive, so they do not need to lose or gain any extra electrons to fill up their ____ shells.
e: The electronic structures of noble gases are very stable and unreactive, so they do not need to lose or gain any extra electrons to fill up their outermost shells. Outermost is the idea that completes this fact.

q: In forming a chemical bond, atoms gain, lose or share electrons in such a way to attain the stable electronic structures of the noble gases, which is known as the ____ Rule.
e: In forming a chemical bond, atoms gain, lose or share electrons in such a way to attain the stable electronic structures of the noble gases, which is known as the Octet Rule. Octet is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Exception is that helium has only two outer electrons, known as a ____ electron configuration.
e: Exception is that helium has only two outer electrons, known as a duplet electron configuration. Duplet is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An ion is formed when an atom loses or gains electrons, so that it has a ____ on it.
e: An ion is formed when an atom loses or gains electrons, so that it has a charge on it. Charge is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Metals tend to lose electrons to form positively charged ions called ____.
e: Metals tend to lose electrons to form positively charged ions called cations. Cations is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Non-metals tend to gain electrons to form negatively charged ions called ____.
e: Non-metals tend to gain electrons to form negatively charged ions called anions. Anions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: An ionic bond is formed when there is complete transfer of an electron or electrons from one atom to another resulting in the formation of cations and ____.
e: An ionic bond is formed when there is complete transfer of an electron or electrons from one atom to another resulting in the formation of cations and anions. Anions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: These oppositely charged ions are held together by a force of electrostatic attraction known as ____ bond.
e: These oppositely charged ions are held together by a force of electrostatic attraction known as ionic bond. An ionic bond forms when electrons transfer and opposite ions attract.

q: This kind of bond occurs mainly between a metal and a ____.
e: This kind of bond occurs mainly between a metal and a non-metal. Non-metal is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A covalent bond is formed by the sharing of electron between two atoms by weak intermolecular forces of ____.
e: A covalent bond is formed by the sharing of electron between two atoms by weak intermolecular forces of attraction. Attraction is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Covalent bonds are formed when non-metal reacts with one ____.
e: Covalent bonds are formed when non-metal reacts with one another. Another is the idea that completes this fact.

q: When two pairs of electrons are shared, a ____ covalent bond is formed.
e: When two pairs of electrons are shared, a double covalent bond is formed. Double is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ionic compounds do not contain molecules; they consist of aggregates of oppositely charged ____.
e: Ionic compounds do not contain molecules; they consist of aggregates of oppositely charged ions. Ions is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Covalent compounds consist of ____.
e: Covalent compounds consist of molecules. Molecules is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ionic compounds are solids and do not ____ easily.
e: Ionic compounds are solids and do not vaporise easily. Vaporise is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Simple covalent compounds are gases or volatile ____.
e: Simple covalent compounds are gases or volatile liquids. Liquids is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous ____.
e: Ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten or in aqueous solution. A solution is a homogeneous mixture of solute dissolved in solvent.

q: Most of simple covalent compounds do not conduct ____.
e: Most of simple covalent compounds do not conduct electricity. Electricity is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Most ionic compounds have high melting points and high ____ points.
e: Most ionic compounds have high melting points and high boiling points. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: Simple covalent compounds have low melting points and low ____ points.
e: Simple covalent compounds have low melting points and low boiling points. Boiling is liquid to gas throughout the liquid at the boiling point.

q: Most ionic compounds are soluble in water but not usually soluble in organic solvents such as toluene, ether, ____, etc.
e: Most ionic compounds are soluble in water but not usually soluble in organic solvents such as toluene, ether, benzene, etc. Benzene is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Simple covalent compounds are usually ____ in water and soluble in covalent organic solvents.
e: Simple covalent compounds are usually insoluble in water and soluble in covalent organic solvents. Insoluble is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Table salt, baking soda, milk of magnesia, limestone, chalk, marble, and rust are examples of ____ compounds.
e: Table salt, baking soda, milk of magnesia, limestone, chalk, marble, and rust are examples of ionic compounds. Ionic is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Methane, hydrochloric acid, water and ammonia are some examples of ____ compounds.
e: Methane, hydrochloric acid, water and ammonia are some examples of covalent compounds. Covalent is the idea that completes this fact.

q: A charged particle is an ____.
e: A charged particle is an ion. Ion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Cation is a positively charged ____.
e: Cation is a positively charged ion. Ion is the idea that completes this fact.

q: Anion is a negatively charged ____.
e: Anion is a negatively charged ion. Ion is the idea that completes this fact.
